title: High-cutoff finite harmonic coarse-Schur stress reaches a residual-reuse boundary
question: Does the exact two-block harmonic coarse-Schur assembly remain reusable at the high oscillator cutoffs of R-416 when every R-425 beta, orientation, tail and block rule is held fixed?
method: Reuse the hash-pinned R-419 conditional law, R-416 log-domain reconstruction, R-422 residual basis and R-425 harmonic split without changing model parameters.
Evaluate volume two at cutoff dimensions 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 30 and 32 for beta 1/2, 2 and 8 and for right and left orientations, retaining every conditional and support-eligibility boundary.
Compare the R-422 residual gap with a separately reconstructed direct block-mean-zero residual gap under the fixed 5e-7 comparison tolerance; do not clip or relax a mismatch.
Run a non-importing reversible Schur control, hostile input/support/singularity mutations, the integrated verifier and Lean R426 scalar bookkeeping cross-check.
finding: The primary lane reaches V=2, d=16, beta=8, right orientation, conditional row 7 with core/tail sizes 7/9 after 1175 assertions. The R-422 residual gap is 5.363184967163699 and the direct residual gap is 5.363188350047810, giving an absolute difference 3.382884111502449e-06, which exceeds the fixed 5e-7 tolerance. The primary verdict is FAIL_ROUTE_LOCAL. The independent control passes 28/28 abstract reversible fixtures and records FAIL_ROUTE_LOCAL_EXPECTED; the hostile lane rejects 7/7 mutations; the integrated verifier passes 15/15; Lean R426 compiles.
decision_reason: The exact high-cutoff residual representations do not agree at the declared audit tolerance. The disagreement is retained as a route-local finite construction/conditioning boundary rather than hidden by a larger tolerance or promoted to a uniform theorem.
decision_scope: Finite volume-two high-cutoff Schur/residual-reuse stress only; no tier change and no physical promotion.
boundary: This is a T0 claim-nonbearing route-local numerical failure. It does not establish gaplessness, a universal no-go, regulator dependence of the theory, or any common-core, history, OS/KMS/GNS, sector, continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang--Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
next_action: Reconcile the R-422 harmonic residual and direct residual basis/precision conventions at high cutoff under an explicit contract, rerun with the unchanged 5e-7 tolerance, and only then revisit an analytic common-core estimate.

adversarial_review.check: The 5e-7 comparison tolerance is not relaxed and the 3.382884111502449e-06 mismatch is not hidden.
The direct residual is independently reconstructed; no basis, precision or conditioning repair is assumed after the disagreement.
The failing row is recorded as V=2, d=16, beta=8, right, row 7 with core/tail 7/9; no left-row substitution is made.
No clipping, upward rounding or forged Schur envelope is used.
The route-local mismatch is not interpreted as a cutoff-uniform no-go or a physical gap statement.
No Hamiltonian, OS/KMS/GNS, sector, Yang--Mills or mass-gap conclusion is inferred.

no_overclaim: The finite residual-reuse mismatch is a reproducible route-local boundary, not a universal theorem or physical no-go. It only identifies the next repair target.
